Open the old oak door and step into Truro’s hidden secret: The Alverton Hotel. Offering unrivalled hospitality, luxurious rooms, two AA rosette-awarded food and delicious tipples, The Alverton is a hop, skip and jump away from Cornwall’s best attractions and most beautiful destinations. Our Rooms Within walking distance of everything that Truro has to offer, The Alverton makes the perfect base for exploring Cornwall. Previously a convent, the four silver star hotel is a historic grade II* listed building which oozes romance and curiosity. With its own bell tower, slate roof, arched mullioned windows, ivy clad walls and curved archways uncovering hidden hideaways - The Alverton offers a unique charm that makes staying here a real experience. More Our Rooms The Courtyard Arched doorways, original flagstone flooring and exposed brickwork complement bespoke furnishings using the finest materials from some of the world's top designer brands. Set a short distance from the main hotel and surrounded by blissful birdsong, The Courtyard promises the ultimate laid-back luxury. More Food and Drink Bar & Restaurant Read more "It's like a refined country house but without an ounce of stuffiness. This laid-back vibe is generated by the delightful members of staff and the elegant but relaxed interior. The décor blends soft neutral tones with touches of Cornish texture, including slate-grey fabrics and oak accents." Julie Bayley, The Scotsman "Up a hill, a short stroll from the centre of Truro, The Alverton has a holy feel about it." The Times Travel "Although it's smack-dab in town, it feels like a genteel country house hotel, complete with rolling, private grounds. From the extraordinary vaulted ceiling of the cathedral-like chapel to the “nuns' cells” in the lower part of the main building, the sandstone and flint buildings ooze historical vibes." Manor Magazine "A hidden gem, really; inside The Alverton it feels grown up and comfortable, with discreet service should you wish. Years of history... The Alverton was once a convent many moons ago. Therefore, our hotel has a fascinating timeline. Delve back in time with us as we explore our Cornish roots. Find out how the beautiful four-silver star hotel that welcomes thousands of visitors and locals each year for a little slice of laid-back luxury came to be. Let’s take a trip back in time! Our story begins with Mr William Tweedy... 1830 The East wing of The Alverton Manor was built for William Tweedy of Truro Vean as a family home in the early 1830s. The Tweedys were a family of repute within the small society of Truro. Senior partners in the Cornish Bank, steadfast supporters of the Tory interest in the town and respected members of the town Corporation. Certainly, The Alverton Manor, with its large garden, was an indication of the prosperity of a “rising” family. The grounds provided William’s thirteen children with an ample play area. William Tweedy, a keen gardener, acted as President of the Royal Horticultural Society for Cornwall from the mid 1830s until his death a quarter of a century later in 1859. After that, the gardens he laid were still open to the public over a decade later. The Bank of Cornwall 1859 Sadly, William Tweedy passed away. Subsequently, the manor house became partly owned by The Bank of Cornwall. Their profits (and later losses) were linked closely with the tin mining industry. 1874 After centuries of dominance, the Cornish tin industry was challenged by cheaper imports. The Cornish Bank loaned money to many mines. As a result, the bank accumulated a series of bad debts due to the closure of those mines. Therefore, confidence in the bank was dented. An anxious search for a body to come to its rescue ensued. However, no help was forthcoming. The bank underwent an audit, and was found to be insolvent. In due course, it was liquidated. Written by sophie Read more articles Continue to eliminate single-use plastic and go greener Reducing our waste and avoiding single-use plastic is something we are passionate about at The Alverton. You only have to gaze across our beautiful private gardens or go for a walk along the Cornish coast to see how important the enviroment is to everyone in Cornwall. Whilst we think we’ve made a good start by introducing refillable glass water bottles in all our rooms to replace plastic earlier in 2019, as well as eliminating plastic straws and pens, we know we can do more! This year one of our resolutions is to replace all the plastic toiletry bottles used in our rooms, and replace these with ceramic bottles created by a local potter. We’ll be following in the footsteps of our sister hotel, The Greenbank, who have already initiated this plastic-free scheme. Read more about it here. Bring Truro an amazing array of events for 2020 One of the most exciting things going on at The Alverton in 2020 is our full calendar of events in The Great Hall. 2019 saw some great successes, including our Murder on the Dancefloor immersive night and the Beer and Cornish Drinks Festival. Keep your eyes peeled for a diary full of themed parties, drinks festivals and live music. The Great Hall venue will be kicking the year off with the Gin and Cornish Drinks Festival, and tickets are on sale now via Eventbrite. More charity work with our new partnership 2019 was our busiest year yet in terms of charity work. This year we are determined to raise even more money. We are so excited to announce our partnership with Cornwall Community Foundation as our charity of the year. This organisation works with thousands of local community groups and charities in Cornwall, from food banks and mental health support centres to children’s youth clubs, elderly social events and Cornish beach cleans.
